method: Two independent blind drafts (A: All documents were screened by title, agency and type; abstracts were read for every document outside clearly irrelevant boilerplate series (SEC SRO filings, FAA airworthiness directives, NPS repatriation notices, FERC filings, sanctions, FTZ, disaster and flood notices), and full text was pulled from govinfo where titles were generic and for every flag and trap candidate (food additives/colors, meat and candy labeling, pecan/apple/corn crops and pesticides, SNAP, plant labor and trucking). Flags are limited to items that change what Brightside must do or change its suppliers' rules or its SNAP-driven demand; traps are the closest look-alikes (other crops/products, individual exemptions, paperwork renewals, meetings, withdrawals). Deadline quotes are verbatim from each document's DATES section. | B: Listed every document (title, agency, type, abstract) in the week file, read each one, and ran a supplementary keyword scan only as a cross-check. Fetched full text from govinfo for every candidate and for the major lookalikes. Flagged only documents that change Brightside's own obligations or meaningfully shift its supplier or customer demand.) reconciled by a third blind agent: agreements kept and merged; every disagreement re-read in full text on govinfo against the profile; genuine 50/50 calls dropped; one-sided traps kept only if they look relevant at first glance; every flag quote re-validated verbatim against the source.
